chunks: Saad narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Kulayni from Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Nakhai from Shahawihi ibn Abdullah al-Jallab who said:

I used to narrate from Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) regarding his son Abu Ja'far, reports that indicated his [Imamate]; but when Abu Ja'far passed away, I became anxious about that and remained bewildered, neither advancing nor retreating, and I feared writing to him about it not knowing what would happen. So I wrote to him asking for supplication and that Allah Almighty relieve us from the causes of distress from the ruler which we had regarding our youths. The reply came with the supplication and the youths were returned to us, and he wrote at the end of the letter: 'You wanted to ask about the successor after the passing of Abu Ja'far, and you were anxious about that, so do not be grieved, for Allah does not misguide a people after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should guard against. Your master after me is Abu Muhammad, my son, and with him is what you need. Allah brings forward what He wills and delays what He wills: [Quran 2:106] I have written that which contains explanation and satisfaction for one of sound intellect.'
Whatever verses We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or like it.
I have written that which contains explanation and satisfaction for one of sound intellect.
ai.seo_question: Who is the successor of Imam al-Askari (a.s.) after the death of his son Abu Ja'far?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* addresses the critical Shia theological issue of the 'Minority of Abu Ja'far' (al-Dawlatayn), where the uncertainty of the Imamate was resolved by Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) confirming his son Abu Muhammad as the successor. The Imam cites Quran 2:106 to illustrate that the temporary concealment or death of an apparent heir is a divine test, ensuring that the true Imam remains the source of guidance and that the community is not left astray after having been guided.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 168 - Saad and Ali bin Muhammad Kulaini have narrated from Ishaq bin Muhammad Nakhai from Shawiya bin Abdullah Jallab that he said:

I previously narrated a report from Imam Hadi (a.s) about his son, Abu Ja’far, which proved his Imamate; but when Abu Ja’far passed away from the world, I was so astonished and bewildered that I did not know what to do and I was in a dilemma and I feared writing to the Imam about it. At last, I wrote a letter to the Imam asking him for supplication to Almighty Allah to save us from the hardships imposed on us from the ruler with regard to our youth. Reply to the letter came with a supplication of the Imam and the difficulty of our youth was also solved. At the end of the letter, the Imam had written: You wanted to ask me about the successor after the death of Abu Ja’far (Muhammad) and you are anxious due to that. Don’t be: “It is not (attributable to) Allah that He should lead a people astray after He has guided them; He even makes clear to them what they should guard against.” [9:115] Your leader after me is Abu Muhammad (Askari), my son. He has everything, which they need. God brings forward whatever He wishes and delays whatever He wishes: Whatever communications We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or like it. [2:106] In this is a clear explanation and convincing proof for one who has a watchful disposition.
